incident-bot: [ALERT] Route53 health checks -> ELB target-group 'inference-usw2a' reporting high 5xx and connection reset rate. Detected at 2026-03-15T02:14:27Z. Paging oncall
Pete (oncall): I'm on it. pulling metrics now. can someone confirm customer impact?
Maya (sre): I see spike in ELB 502/504s for us-west-2a, increased latency to inference edge nodes. CloudWatch shows TargetResponseTime up ~700ms and TargetHealth unhealthy count 23/60.
Alexa (net): Route53 weighted routing shows traffic pinned to us-west-2a for some customers (weight 70). DNS TTL was 300s last change — might be sticky caches.
Dan (runtime): Service side: redis KV cache on inference-gw-usw2a is overloaded, error rate from model workers up. KV miss + long tail GC -> 502s.
Kim (product): Customer-facing: a few customers reported errors in logs and mobile clients seeing 502. Support paged Jorge. Any P0s?
Jorge (support): Two enterprise customers reporting >10% errors for requests to hosted endpoints in us-west-2. They're impacted. Ticket open.
Pete (oncall): ok declaring incident: INC-2026-309. SLO risk. Initiating mitigation plan. Maya, you own infra fixes. Alexa, network routing. Dan, runtime fallback. Kim/Jorge handle comms.
Maya (sre): Action 1: remove unhealthy targets from target-group to stop bad traffic. Running: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0abc1234` (iterating).
Maya (sre): Action 2: scale up inference pool in us-west-2b/c and open burst capacity. `asg set-desired-capacity` executed + verifying.
Alexa (net): Action 3: reduce Route53 weight for us-west-2a from 70 -> 10 and shift 60 weight to us-west-2b, 30 to us-west-2c. Applying change with low TTL (60s). Making change now.
deploy-bot: Route53 change requested by Alexa (net). Change ID: Z3ABCDEF123. Propagation expected ~30-90s for our checks.
Dan (runtime): Action 4: enable canary fallback to smaller model variant (low-memory runtime) in all zones. Pushing config: `service config set inference-fallback=true --zone all`. Rolling restarts on canary nodes.
Maya (sre): Observing target health after deregister: unhealthy count dropping to 8. ELB 5xx rate decreasing.
Pete (oncall): Are there any stuck client-side connections causing resets? Alexa?
Alexa (net): Some carrier networks still hitting old IPs due to cached DNS entries and long client TTLs. We're seeing ~12% of traffic still to old AZ for certain prefixes. Working w/Cloudfront to purge route caches.
Kim (product): Drafting status update for customers: short blurb + ETA to recovery. Will post to status.redwood.inference once we have steady metrics for 10m.
Jorge (support): Logged workaround for affected customers: switch to dedicated region or retry logic with exponential backoff for 60s. Sending to enterprise contacts now.
Maya (sre): Running deeper: EBS IO waits spiking on some instances in 2a, likely causing worker stalls. Spun up replacement instances and attached new volumes. Continuing data sync.
Dan (runtime): Runtime metrics: model queue backlog down 40% since scale-up and canary enabled. Error rate trending down from 11% -> 3% in last 5m.
Alexa (net): Route53 weights applied. I'm seeing global health check flapping for 2a still but traffic shift completed for our control-plane. Some providers remain sticky.
Pete (oncall): Good progress. Maya/Dan keep monitoring for 15m. Kim/Jorge prepare customer comms; tag customers with irreversible SLA exposure.
Maya (sre): Enabling proactive ELB connection drain on remaining instances in 2a: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30` to speed drains.
Dan (runtime): If we still see errors after shift, plan B is to cut traffic to us-west-2a completely and failover to us-east-1 read replicas. That's a high-latency fallback but safe.
Pete (oncall): Any indications of related control-plane events (EC2 API, EBS limits)?
Maya (sre): No control-plane throttle. This looks localized to AZ EBS performance + ELB target overload. No region-wide outage.
Alexa (net): Cross-check: Route53 health checks show elevated latency for 2a region from 4 vantage points. Edge proxies showing connreset spikes for TCP sessions originating from certain ISP ranges.
Kim (product): Support-facing status posted: "Partial degradation in us-west-2 affecting hosted inference endpoints; engineers are mitigating with traffic shift and instance replacements. Next update in 15 minutes."
Pete (oncall): Marking incident severity as Sev2. Creating postmortem placeholder. Recording timeline.
Jorge (support): Customer A (ID: C-4821) in EU reported errors earlier; I confirmed retrying succeeded after 90s. They want timeline and RCA.
Maya (sre): Monitoring: 10m moving average 5xx rate now 1.1% (was 11%). Targeting under 0.5% for full recovery.
Dan (runtime): Runtime logs: sample stacktrace for 502s from model worker: ```
Error: upstream write failed: connection reset by peer
    at model_server.js:452:22
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
```
Alexa (net): Suggest we add a follow-up: lower default Route53 TTL from 300 -> 60 for critical endpoint groups to allow faster failover next time. Filing infra task.
Pete (oncall): Agree. Add to action items. Who will own? Maya?
Maya (sre): I'll own TTL/weighting runbook updates and a post-incident checklist for EBS replacement pattern.
Kim (product): I'll prepare customer-facing RCA draft after postmortem. Need timeline + impact numbers.
Pete (oncall): OK. Wrapping: we'll keep thread open for 60m. If stable for 30m and 5xx <0.5% we'll move to monitoring. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-309 status: mitigation in progress. Metrics OK threshold not yet met.
Pete (oncall): last note: keep notes of commands run here for postmortem. I'll capture console logs and attach to the RCA."
